input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across calls, so concurrent or nested awaits of the same decorated coroutine corrupt each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: the same @retry-decorated coroutine is awaited concurrently in asyncio tasks, or it awaits itself recursively. Each call runs stats.clear() on the same dict that other in-flight calls read and write through their local statistics, so one call's attempt counts and timings are reset or mixed with another's. Impact: statistics observed by callers are silently wrong.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is cleared and reused on every call, so concurrent or nested calls overwrite and mix each other's attempt counts and timings. It only covers the async wrapper, but the label explicitly includes concurrent awaits of the async wrapper, so this is the same defect.
